name: Turn new blog posts into a post per platform with OpenAI and Ampost

parameters.content:
## Turn new blog posts into a post per platform
### How it works
When your blog publishes, this workflow reads the article and asks Ampost which of your platforms can take it: Ampost's platform rules give each platform's character limit and whether it needs an image (the article's og:image is used). OpenAI writes a separate text for each platform within its limit. Ampost then checks the post against your connected accounts. Platforms that fail (no account, too long, no image) are left out, and the rest go into your Ampost queue. You get an email that says what was queued and why any platform was skipped.

### Setup
1. Install the community node **n8n-nodes-ampost** (tested with 0.1.1) on n8n 2.48.7: Settings → Community nodes → Install, as in the [n8n guide](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/). Until n8n verifies it, the node needs self-hosted n8n.
2. Create an Ampost credential with an API key from [ampost.io](https://ampost.io/?ref=n8n) → Setup → API keys, and connect your accounts there.
3. Add queue slots in Ampost (Queue), or set **whenToPost** to `draft` to review posts in Ampost first.
4. Add OpenAI and SMTP credentials.
5. Set your feed URL in **New blog post**, and the platforms, voice and email in **Settings**.

### Good to know
Each article is posted once: **Skip posted articles** remembers links. Swap the email node for Slack if you prefer.

### 1. Read the article
New feed items, minus ones already posted. The page gives the og:image, and Ampost gives each platform's rules.

### 2. Write a post per platform
Only platforms that can take this article. OpenAI writes within each limit; anything over is cut at a word.

### 3. Check with Ampost and queue
Ampost checks the post against your accounts. Failing platforms are dropped; an empty queue means a draft.

### 4. Email a report
What was queued, what was skipped and why, including AI or Ampost errors.
